title: Using agents to build an agent company: Joao Moura
talk_summary: This is a CrewAI founder's conference keynote: growth stats, his personal story of building marketing and lead-qualification crews, and product announcements (code execution flag, crew training CLI, third-party agent interop, CrewAI Plus hosting). It contains almost no engineering mechanism detail and is largely marketing.

takeaways.technique: Role-specialized crews with a chief/editor agent on top
takeaways.what_they_do: Composes small crews of named specialist roles (content creator, analyst, senior writer) plus a chief officer agent that reviews and finalizes output, rather than one generalist agent.
takeaways.evidence_quote: a content creator specialist a social media analyst a senior content writer and a chief content officer bring them out together
takeaways.numbers: claims 10x more views in 16 days (unverified, marketing)

takeaways.technique: Start simple, expand to low-risk high-impact automations
takeaways.what_they_do: Sequences automation rollout: ship one narrow crew, verify it works, then add the next lower-risk/higher-impact one instead of building the whole org upfront.
takeaways.evidence_quote: start simple expend to low risk and high impact that's what we did

takeaways.technique: Train-the-crew CLI baking instructions into agent memory
takeaways.what_they_do: A CLI command takes natural-language instructions and persists them into the agents' memory so future runs produce consistent behavior.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can give instructions to it and that's going to become baked into the memory of your agents

takeaways.what_they_do: A single flag lets agents write and run code as a tool instead of requiring pre-built tools.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all you got to do it's one flag allow code execution that works your agents can code now
